# Overview

This site documents the analytical work behind a study of metabolic syndrome in
a population-based cohort. The work has two connected parts.

The first is a **Composite Metabolic Desirability Index (CMDI)**: a continuous
measure of metabolic risk built from body mass index, triglycerides, HDL
cholesterol and fasting glucose using multi-response optimisation and desirability
functions. The motivation is that the conventional International Diabetes
Federation definition reduces a graded biological phenomenon to a yes/no
classification, which discards information at the thresholds and treats all
qualifying criteria as interchangeable.

The second is a **clinical prediction model** for that index, fitted with a
bespoke priority-ordered variable selection procedure (`bootPriorProc`) across a
set of data domains spanning demographics, dietary indices, physical activity,
medication, device-based body composition, clinical biochemistry, targeted
metabolomics, urinary metabolites and untargeted lipidomics.

# Sections

## Index reconstruction

[Reconstructing the CMDI after a triglyceride data correction](cmdi_tg_correction_diagnostic.qmd)

A data-quality problem was identified in the triglyceride measurements after the
initial analysis was complete. Because triglycerides are one of the four
components of the CMDI, the correction propagates into the model outcome rather
than into a single predictor.

This section documents the diagnostics used to decide how the index should be
constructed before committing to a refit. It compares the original index, the
index with corrected triglycerides, and a version with fixed clinical bounds;
examines the consequences of deriving desirability bounds from the observed data
range; and records the alternative parameterisations that were tested and set
aside.

# Data

The analysis set comprises repeated observations from participants measured at
two timepoints. Variables are organised into blocks reflecting how they were
collected and how readily they are obtained in practice, and this ordering is
used by the selection procedure so that lower-priority molecular measurements
have to earn their place against routinely available clinical ones.

| Block | Contents |
|---|---|
| `demo` | Demographics |
| `bp` | Blood pressure sub-index |
| `activity` | Accelerometry-derived physical activity |
| `dietary` | Dietary indices |
| `meds` | Medication use |
| `human` | Device-based body composition and function |
| `biochem` | Clinical biochemistry |
| `aas` | Amino acids and sugars |
| `acylCar` | Acylcarnitines |
| `hilic` | Urinary metabolites (HILIC) |
| `ttp` | Tyrosine–tryptophan pathway metabolites |
| `lip` | Untargeted lipidomics |

# Software

Analyses are carried out in R. The index is constructed with `desirability2`;
model fitting and validation use the `rms` package, with bootstrap resampling
clustered by participant to respect the repeated-measures structure. Missing
values are imputed by random forest (`miceRanger`). This site is built with
Quarto.

# Notes

Pages are added as sections of the analysis are completed. Numerical results
shown here are internal working outputs and should not be treated as final until
the corresponding model refits have been run and checked.
